name: Najam Gohar
role: Postdoctoral Fellow, Section of Digestive Diseases
tagline: Physician-researcher working on cardiovascular, cardiometabolic, and metabolic liver disease outcomes with real-world clinical data.
profile: Najam Gohar is a physician-researcher and Postdoctoral Fellow at Yale School of Medicine with experience in cardiovascular outcomes research, clinical epidemiology, real-world evidence, large-scale health data, multi-omics, and scientific writing. He uses Python, R, SQL, and statistical software across All of Us, Truveta, TriNetX, UK Biobank, HCUP NIS, and CDC WONDER.

experience.org: Yale School of Medicine, Section of Digestive Diseases
bullets: Analyze electronic health record, survey, physical-measurement, genomic, RNA-seq, and proteomic data in the All of Us Researcher Workbench using Python, R, SQL, Jupyter notebooks, and the OMOP Common Data Model.
Build longitudinal cohorts and phenotype definitions in Truveta; perform data cleaning, propensity-score matching, survival analysis, and predictive modeling.

Support metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease and chronic liver disease studies through quantitative and multi-omic analysis, bench-based research, literature review, manuscript development, and scientific presentations.
Select and learn software according to each research question, adapting workflows across data platforms and statistical environments.

Design and conduct retrospective cohort studies using TriNetX, HCUP NIS, CDC WONDER, and other large health datasets across cardiovascular, cardiometabolic, gastrointestinal, hematologic, and oncologic conditions.
Define exposures, outcomes, covariates, and subgroups; conduct regression, propensity-score, time-to-event, and sensitivity analyses; and translate findings into manuscripts and conference abstracts.
Coordinate collaborative projects from research-question development through analysis, interpretation, journal submission, and responses to peer review.

experience.org: Lahore General Hospital and Pakistan Institute of Neurosciences

education.degree: Bachelor of Medicine, Bachelor of Surgery (MBBS)

skills.label: Programming and analysis
skills.value: Python, R, SQL, Stata, SPSS, and Joinpoint

skills.label: Clinical data platforms
skills.value: All of Us Researcher Workbench, Truveta, TriNetX, UK Biobank, HCUP National Inpatient Sample, and CDC WONDER

skills.label: Biomedical data
skills.value: Electronic health records, administrative data, surveys, physical measurements, genomics, RNA-seq, proteomics, genotype-linked clinical outcomes, and multimodal clinical data

skills.label: Methods
skills.value: Retrospective cohort design, phenotype definition, propensity-score matching, logistic and linear regression, Kaplan-Meier and survival analysis, subgroup and sensitivity analyses, predictive modeling, and model evaluation

skills.label: Evidence synthesis
skills.value: Systematic reviews, diagnostic test accuracy studies, meta-analysis, and meta-regression using R, RevMan, and PRISMA methods

skills.label: Scientific communication
skills.value: Manuscript development, conference abstracts, presentations, publication-ready tables and figures, journal submissions, and responses to reviewers

skills.label: Technical adaptability
skills.value: Rapid evaluation and adoption of new software, analytical tools, and research platforms according to project needs

service.org: IHME Global Burden of Disease Study
service.detail: Contribute to collaborative population-health research on global disease burden and health trends.
Review manuscripts for Frontiers in Immunology, Frontiers in Medicine, Scientific Reports, Frontiers in Nutrition, and Frontiers in Cellular and Infection Microbiology.
Mentor early-career researchers in study design, database analysis, scientific writing, and publication development.

leadership.org: AMCotomy Surgery Interest Group, Ameer-ud-Din Medical College
leadership.detail: Organized the college’s inaugural suturing workshop for more than 300 medical students and secured donated materials and sponsorship support.
Managed budgets and financial operations for research workshops and mentorship activities.

volunteering: Held coordination and volunteer roles with the Ameer-ud-Din Patient Welfare Society, Ameer-ud-Din Child Education Program, Blood Donation Society, and Humanity Still Exists medical outreach program.

news.title: Joined Yale University as a Postdoctoral Research Fellow
news.summary: Najam announced on LinkedIn that he has joined Yale University as a Postdoctoral Research Fellow, working on metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD), one of the fastest-growing causes of liver cancer worldwide.

news.title: Welcome New Faculty, Staff, and Postdocs in the Yale Department of Internal Medicine (August 2026)
news.summary: The Department of Internal Medicine welcomed its new faculty, staff, and postdoctoral associates and fellows for August 2026. The list includes Najam Gohar, MBBS, as a new postdoctoral fellow in the Section of Digestive Diseases.
